column2: That wife of Kardama, of the Prajapati Pulaha's line... Satyanetra, Havya, Apa, Murti, Shanaishchara,
and Soma the fifth of them were in the Svayambhuva interval; the five Atreyas are renowned, gone by with the Yama gods.
Their sons and grandsons, of the great-souled Atreyas, passed away in the Svayambhuva interval by hundreds and thousands.
On Priti, wife of Pulastya, Dattagni was his son; in his former birth he is remembered as Agastya in the Svayambhuva interval.
The middle was Devabahu, and the one named Atri: those three. The youngest of them, famed as Sadvati,
the radiant mother of Parjanya, and the auspicious wife of Agni are remembered; and of the Brahmin sage Paulastya, the wise son of Priti,
the wife Sujangha bore many sons from Dana; they are famed and remembered as the Paulastyas in the Svayambhuva interval.
Kshama bore the sons of the Prajapati Pulastya, all with the radiance of the Treta fire, whose fame is established:
Kardama, Urvarivan and Sahishnu: those three; the sage Kanakapitha and the auspicious daughter Pivari.
Kardama's wife Shruti, the Atreyi, herself bore a son named Shankhapada and a daughter Kamya.
That glorious Shankhapada, a world-guardian and Prajapati, was devoted to the southern direction; Kamya was given to Priyavrata.
Kamya obtained from Priyavrata ten sons equal to the Svayambhuva and two daughters, by whom Kshatra was set going.
Yashodhara bore Kanakapitha's famed son named Sahishnu; the slender-waisted bore Kamadeva.
Sannati bore Kratu's auspicious sons equal to Kratu; they have neither wife nor son, all being of upward seed.
Those sixty thousand are heard of as the Valakhilyas; they go in front of Aruna, surrounding the day-maker,
all until the dissolution of beings, companions of the winged ones. Their two younger sisters, holy and Satyavati,
daughters-in-law of Parvasha, and of the son Purnamasa. On Urja, Vasishtha's wife, seven Vasishthas were born.
Their elder sister was Pundarika, slender-waisted, mother of the radiant Prana, his dear queen.
The seven younger Vasishthas of hers are famed: Rakshas, Garta, Urdhvabahu, Savana and Pavana,
Sutapa and Sankuri: all these are remembered as the seven sages. Ratna bore the fair-limbed, famed Markandeyi
in the western direction, the king and Prajapati Ketuman. The gotras of these great-souled Vasishthas are by names.
Those of the past in the Svayambhuva interval, now hear of Agni's, creatures. Thus the creation of sages has been told with its continuation.
Hearing that, the death of Sati, the god, the trident-bearer Shankara, knowing as it was the dialogue between the two and with Daksha and the sages, the revered lord grew angry.
Rudra said: "Of all the worlds, Bhurloka is called first; I shall always bear it by the command of the Supreme Lord.
On this earth all shining worlds stand supported; I bear them always, and by his command.
The gods' four varnas eat together; I shall not eat with them; then they will give separately.
Since Sati, innocent, was disregarded for my sake, Daksha, and all your other daughters were praised with their husbands,
therefore when the Vaivasvata interval arrives, these great sages will again be born, in my second sacrifice, not from a womb.
When Brahma's semen was offered, in the Chakshusha Manu's interval, having proclaimed all of them, he cursed Daksha again:
'You will be a human king in the line of Chakshusha, grandson of Prachinabarhis and son of the Prachetases.
Daksha by name here, you will be born on Marisha, the daughter of trees, when the Vaivasvata interval arrives.
There too I shall make an obstacle for you, evil-minded, in your dharma-joined work, one hard to approach.'"
Suta said: Hearing that, Daksha cursed Rudra in turn: "Since for my sake you did what was harmful to the sages, therefore the twice-born will not sacrifice to you together with the gods at sacrifice.
The cruel one's oblations they will offer and touch water in rites; you will stay right here, leaving heaven until the yuga's end."
Then he is not worshipped with the gods but separately. Daksha, cursed by Rudra of immeasurable brilliance,
abandoning the Svayambhuva body, was born among humans here.
Knowing the householder-lord of sacrifices, the Daksha performed that sacrifice with all together with the deities.
Then the goddess Sati, when the Vaivasvata interval came, the mountain-king begot on Mena that goddess Uma.
The goddess who was Sati before afterwards became Uma; she is Bhava's wife always, and Bhava is not freed from her.
Like Aditi devoted to Marichi's Kashyapa, like Shri to Narayana, like Shachi to Maghavan,
Kirti to Vishnu, ... and Arundhati to Vasishtha: these goddesses never leave these husbands.
Returning in kalpas they are born with them again. Thus Daksha son of Prachetas was born in the Chakshusha interval;
again the king, on Marisha from the ten Prachetases, was born by that curse as the second, so we have heard.
The seven great sages headed by Bhrigu were born in the first Treta yuga of Manu Vaivasvata formerly,
in the sacrifice of the great god, bearing the Varuni body. This was the regret following the two in another birth,
of the Prajapati Daksha and of the wise Tryambaka; therefore one should never nurse regret in quarrels here.
Even one gone to another birth, being affected by good and bad, a creature does not lose the renown; the wise should not do that.
Thus this story removing sin has been followed through, which you formerly set going here concerning Daksha.
This story was told in connection with the line of ancestors; now in order of the ancestors I shall tell of the gods.
At the beginning of Treta, formerly, in the Svayambhuva interval, the sons of Yajna famed as the Devayamas,
renowned sons of Brahma, because of unbornness the Ajitas; these are the sons of Svayambhuva, the mind-born called Shaktas.
Whose groups these are, three of the gods are remembered; the thirty-three born of metres, in the creation of Svayambhuva.
Yadu, Yayati... two gods...Vibhasa and Kratu, Prayati, Vishruta, Dyuti,
Vayavya, Samyama: the twelve Yamas are proclaimed; Asama, Ugradrishti, Sunaya, Shuchishrava,
Kevala, Vishvarupa, Sudaksha, Madhupa, Turiya, Idrayuk, Yukta, Gravajit,
Chanima, Vishvadeva, Javishtha, Mitavan, Jara, Vibhu, Vibhava, Richika, Durdiha,
Shruti, Grinana and Brihatshukra: twelve are proclaimed; these were soma-drinkers in the Svayambhuva interval.
These groups were radiant, valiant and very mighty; their Indra then was the lord Vishvabhuk in the first.
The Asuras who then were their heirs and kin, Suparnas, Yakshas, Gandharvas, Pishachas, serpents and Rakshasas —
these eight were with the ancestors, the races of the gods; the Svayambhuva interval's creatures, their thousands, have passed.
Endowed with power and form, with life and strength, they are not told here in detail, lest there be digression.
The creation of Svayambhuva is to be known now; the past is seen by the present, not in the Vaivasvata.
With creatures, deities, sages and ancestors — the seven sages of those who were earlier, understand them:
Bhrigu, Angiras, Marichi, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Atri and Vasishtha: seven in the Svayambhuva interval.
Agnidhra, Agnibahu, Modha, Medhatithi, Vasu, Jyotishman, Dyutiman, Havya, Savana and Sattra:
these ten very mighty sons of Svayambhuva Manu, swift as wind, of great being, were kings in the first interval.
With Asuras, good Gandharvas, Yakshas, serpents, Rakshasas, Pishachas, humans, Suparnas and hosts of Apsarases,
it cannot be told in order even in hundreds of years; because of the multitude of names, how can there be their count in a family?
The creatures named for yugas who were in the Svayambhuva interval have passed with great time, by the order of solstices, years and yugas.
The sages said: "Who is this revered Time, taker of all beings? Whose womb, what beginning, what truth, what nature?
What is his eye, what body, or what limbs are remembered? What name, what is his self? Tell us the truth truly."
Suta said: "Hear the true nature of Time, and having heard, ascertain it. Born of the Sun, beginning with the wink, counting is called his eye.
His body is day and night, and the winks are his limbs. The year is his truth, and his name is of the nature of the kala.
That Prajapati is of the nature of present, future and past time. Understand the state of Time divided fivefold.
By days, fortnights, months, seasons and solstices: first the Samvatsara, second the Parivatsara,
third the Idavatsara, fourth the Anuvatsara, fifth the Vatsara; their time is called the yuga.
I shall tell their truth; hear it as told. The fire called Kratu is considered the Samvatsara.
That Aditeya Sun, the fire of time, is Parivatsara; also the course of bright and dark, the bird made of the essence of waters.
That Soma is the Idavatsara, determined in the Purana; and he who purifies the worlds by seven and seven bodies —
the follower-wind of the world, that Vayu is the Anuvatsara. The lofty Rudra, born of egoism, born of Brahma —
that Rudra is to be known as the Vatsara among them, the dark-red. I shall tell his truth; hear as told.
By union of limbs and sub-limbs, the self of time, the great-grandfather, the womb of Riks, Samans and Yajus, the lord of the five,
he is Agni, Yama and Time, origin, he is Prajapati, declared as the Year; the wise call the Sun the womb.
Since he is the womb of the divisions of time, months, seasons and solstices, of planets and stars, cold, heat, rain, life and actions,
Bhaskara is the womb of divisions and of days; the Vaikarika, serene-souled, Brahma's son, the Prajapati.
One and many, day, month, season, grandfather, Aditya, Savita, Bhanu, Jivana, honoured by Brahma,
origin and imperishable of beings, therefore Bhaskara. The second Parivatsara is to be known as proud of the stars.
Soma is lord of all herbs, therefore he is the great-grandfather, the livelihood of all beings, the Lord who brings about attainment and security.
Looking constantly, he bears the world with his rays, and the tithis, parva junctions, full moons and new moons.
The night-maker is the womb, the immortal-souled Prajapati; therefore Soma, ancestral, is remembered as of the nature of the year.
By prana, apana, samana and the rest, vyana and udana as well, by the actions of creatures in the world he sets all activity in motion.
Of the five senses, mind, intellect, memory and strength-selves, performing the actions at the same time,
the Self of all, lord of all worlds, by Avaha, Pravaha and the rest, he acts by benefits with seven and seven bodies.
The Creator of all beings, always blowing, secure; the womb of fire, of waters, of earth, the accumulation of sun and moon;
Vayu, the Prajapati, being the world-self, great-grandfather. He makes day and night; therefore Vayu is the Anuvatsara.
These four lords of creatures, born of sub-wing(?), are called the ancestors of all worlds, the selves of the worlds.
As Brahma meditated, from his mouth Bhava arose, the sage, Mahadeva, Brahmin, self of beings, great-grandfather.
Ishvara of all beings, who is recited as the Pranava; by entering the self of beings arises the origin of limbs and sub-limbs.
The maddener, the doer of grace, Rudra is called the Vatsara. Sun, moon, fire, wind and Rudra likewise,
proud of the yuga, self of time, constantly the destroyer, the lord. Rudra, the revered one, entered this world with his own brilliance,
by dependence on me, by union, with bodies and names. Then by his valour, the doer of grace to the worlds,
godhood, ancestor-hood and time-hood, what is highest of him. Therefore Rudra is in all ways worshipped by the knowers.
Because he is the revered lord of the Prajapatis, the Prajapati, the cause of becoming of all beings, the Self of all, dark-red.
Rudra again and again restores the herbs when exhausted, by the gods led by Prajapati, rightly desiring the fruit of sacrifice.
With three kapalas, on the exhaustion of herbs, the revered one is worshipped by the Tryambaka (offering), therefore he is called Tryambaka.
Gayatri, Trishtubh and Jagati are remembered as the Tryambakas by name with love, the wombs of the lord of the forest (soma).
By those become one, threefold, by his own valour, the three-means offering with three potsherds is remembered.
The Tryambaka offering is by that Tryambaka remembered. Thus the five-year yuga is told by the wise.
And this fivefold self called Samvatsara by the twice-born... one of six was born, named from Madhu and the other seasons.
Sons of the season, the Artavas, five: thus the creation in brief. Thus this much honoured the lives of beings; like a river's current, unattached, Time runs, destroying.
Their progeny is beyond measure to count, son: sons and grandsons are endless.
One who recites this lineage of the great Prajapatis of meritorious deeds, of holy fame, would obtain great success.
Of the warm, the warm country is remembered; of the purifying, the purifying; of darkness the country is called the dark one.
Of the sage the Maunideshi; of the drum the Dundubhi is remembered. These are the seven radiant countries in Krauncha-dvipa.
Jyotishman had seven very mighty sons in Kushadvipa: Udbhij, Venuman, Vairatha, Lavana, Dhriti,
Prabhakara the sixth, and Kapila the seventh remembered. Udbhij is the first varsha, the second Venumandala,
the third Rathakara, the fourth Lavana, the fifth Dhritiman, the sixth Prabhakara,
the seventh named Kapila after Kapila. Their countries in Kushadvipa bear the same names,
adorned with people possessing the conduct of the ashramas. Vapushman, lord of Shalmala, had seven sons,
Shveta, Harita, Jimuta, Rohita, Vaidyuta, Manasa and Suprabha the seventh.
The country of Shveta is Shveta, Harita's Suharita, of Jimuta Jimuta, of Rohita Rohita,
of Vaidyuta Vaidyuta, of Manasa Manasa, of Suprabha Suprabha: these seven are the country-guardians.
I shall tell of Plakshadvipa, next after Jambudvipa. Medhatithi had seven sons, kings, lords of Plakshadvipa:
the eldest named Shantabhaya, the second Shishira, the third Sukhodaya, the fourth called Nanda,
the fifth Shiva, the sixth called Kshemaka, and the seventh to be known as Dhruva: the sons of Medhatithi are remembered.
By the names of those seven are the seven varshas: Shantabhaya, Shishira, Sukhodaya,
Ananda, Shiva, Kshemaka and Dhruva; those are their seven varshas in portions, alike.
They were settled by them earlier in the Svayambhuva interval by those sons of Medhatithi, the lords of Plakshadvipa.
In Plakshadvipa the people were made possessed of the conduct of varnas and ashramas. In these, from Plakshadvipa to those near Shakadvipa,
in the five, the dharma that divides varnas and ashramas is to be known; happiness, life, beauty, strength and dharma constantly.
In these five continents all means are remembered. Plakshadvipa is passed; understand Jambudvipa.
Priyavrata consecrated Agnidhra, the eldest heir, Kamya's mighty son, as king, lord of Jambudvipa.
He had nine sons equal to Prajapatis; the eldest was famed as Nabhi, his younger Kimpurusha,
Harivarsha the third, the fourth was Ilavrita, Ramya the fifth son, Hiranvan is called the sixth,
Kuru the seventh of them, Bhadrashva remembered as the eighth, Ketumala the ninth; understand their countries.
The father gave Nabhi the southern varsha called Hima; the varsha Hemakuta he gave to Kimpurusha;
the Naishadha, remembered as a varsha, he gave to Harivarsha; the middle one of Sumeru he gave to Ilavrita.
The Nila varsha he gave to Ramya; the northern white one, the father gave to Hiranvat.
The varsha north of Shringavat he gave to Kuru; the Salyavat varsha he assigned to Bhadrashva;
the Gandhamadana varsha he assigned to Ketumala. Thus the nine varshas have been told by me in portions.
Agnidhra consecrated those sons in the varshas, in order, the righteous-souled one; then he stood in austerity.
Thus by these seven the whole of the seven continents was settled, by the sons of Priyavrata and the grandsons of Svayambhuva.
Thus in all the varshas arrangements are made again and again by kings of the sevens, when dissolution has passed.
Such is the nature of kalpas and of the settlement of continents. The eight varshas beginning with Kimpurusha, which are heard of,
their success is natural, mostly happy, without effort; there is no reversal in them, and no fear of old age and death.
There is no dharma and adharma there, nor highest, lowest or middle; there is no order of yugas in any of the eight fields.
I shall tell the creation of Nabhi; understand in this one called Hima. Nabhi begot a son on Merudevi, of great radiance,
Rishabha, best of kings, elder of all Kshatriyas. From Rishabha was born Bharata, a hero, eldest of a hundred sons.
Rishabha, having consecrated his son, stood in great renunciation; he handed the southern varsha called Hima to Bharata.
Therefore the wise know the varsha as Bharata, by his name. Bharata's son was a learned, righteous one named Sumati.
